name: Eye caste system

card.summary: An internet meme that sorts iris colours into a joking hierarchy of tiers, which feeds looksmaxxing talk about eye colour and why some people try to lighten theirs.
card.aka: Men Destined to Define Eras; 1998 eye chart
card.note: A meme ranking, with racial overtones in some versions; eye-colour-change procedures discussed alongside it carry medical risks.

quick.overview:
The eye caste system is an internet meme that assigns social roles to iris colours, from lightest blue at the top to darkest brown at the bottom. It was built on a doll-company chart of eye colours labelled A10 to T50 and became popular in 2019 to 2021.

In looksmaxxing it is used both seriously and ironically as shorthand for the idea that lighter eyes are more attractive, which is one reason eye colour appears in appearance discussions. Know Your Meme calls the meme pseudoscientific, and it is not a measured ranking of anything.
quick.how: People post the chart and state their tier, parody it with other charts (height, energy drinks), or cite it when discussing eye colour. In appearance communities, the discussion sometimes leads to coloured contacts or to eye-colour surgery.
quick.risks: The chart itself carries no physical risk, though versions carry racial hierarchy framing. Press coverage of eye-colour surgery trends in young men describes health risks and mixed results.

lead: The eye caste system is a meme that ranks iris colours into tiers with assigned social roles. It derives from an eye-colour selection chart in a My Twinn custom-doll order catalog, in which shades from light blue to dark brown were labelled A10 to T50 [1].

On June 15, 2019, an anonymous user on 4chan's /pol/ board posted an edited version titled 'The eye caste system', placing A10 at the top as 'Men destined to define eras and change history' and T50 at the bottom as sanitation workers and street sweepers [1]. It went viral on iFunny in February 2021, and users parodied it by swapping in charts about height and energy drinks [1].

Know Your Meme calls the system pseudoscientific and notes that discussion of the chart is both earnest and ironic within Lookism and looksmaxxing discourse [1]. In its looksmaxxing form the chart connects to claims that lighter eyes appeal more to women, which The Daily Beast reports have led some young men to risk their health to change their eye colour [2].

chain: Lighter shades are framed as higher status
Members look at ways to alter or enhance eye colour
angle.text: It does not change the look of the eyes; it is a ranking meme. In looksmaxxing it is used as a reference point when people talk about eye colour and when they consider coloured contacts, makeup or eye-colour procedures to look lighter-eyed.

infobox: My Twinn doll catalog, labelled 1996 or 1998 [1]

paras: The base image came from a My Twinn order form used by buyers to pick a doll's eye colour; the source is dated 1998 on some pages but the form image is labelled Fall 1996 [1]. Versions of the chart circulated as quiz posts from December 2016 on iFunny, Facebook and Reddit before the tiered edit appeared in June 2019 [1].

After spreading on iFunny in 2021, users rated characters and people by iris shade, mostly A10 and T50, and later replaced the chart with others such as height (July 2021) and energy drinks (June 2022) [1].

The tiers run from philosophers, kings and explorers at the top through artists, officers, middle management and labourers to 'untouchables' at the bottom [1]. Know Your Meme describes the format as sitting uncomfortably at the intersection of internet humour and race pseudoscience [1].

The Daily Beast reports that influencers have claimed lighter, typically blue, eyes appeal more to women, and describes a trend it calls 'eye maxxing' in which young men try to change eye colour, with results it calls mixed at best [2]. The meme serves as shorthand in that conversation.
No studies found. The chart is a meme with no scientific basis as a ranking.

timeline.event: Eye chart posted as a quiz image on iFunny [1].
Tiered 'eye caste system' edit posted on 4chan /pol/ [1].
